title: Open Frobenius power squares and assembly of compact exchange pasting
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $p$ prime, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{k_0}$. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $n\geq1$, and set $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$ and $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-$A$ modules on the small pro-etale sites and their adjoint operations $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. All composition comparisons below are the canonical ones of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]; composition is written with the rightmost map first.

Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and fix one compactification $X_0\xrightarrow{j_0}W_0\xrightarrow{p_0}\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, with $j_0$ open and $p_0$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write $X\xrightarrow jW\xrightarrow ps$ for its base change to $k$. Put $g=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, $b=\operatorname{id}_{W_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, $P_r=L(g^r)^*$, $B_r=L(b^r)^*$, $Q_r=L(h^r)^*$, $J=j_!$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero], $R=Rp_*$ and $F=RJ$. Let $c_m:P_1P_m\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{m+1}$, $d_m:B_1B_m\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{m+1}$, $t_m:Q_1Q_m\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{m+1}$ be the inverse composition comparisons. Let $u_r:Q_rR\to RB_r$ be the proper-square exchanges of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] (1). Assume their pasting equation
$$u_{m+1,K}\circ t_{m,RK}=R(d_{m,K})\circ u_{1,B_mK}\circ Q_1(u_{m,K})$$
for every $K\in D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $m\geq1$.

For each $r\geq1$, $jg^r=b^rj$ and the square with vertical edges $j,j$ and horizontal edges $g^r,b^r$ is Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with lift $(g^r,j)$. Each $P_r$ preserves the bounded constructible category $D^b_c(X,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Let $v_r:B_rJ\xrightarrow{\sim}JP_r$ be the canonical open-square exchange of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange], normalized by the identity on the open, and let $e_r=(Rv_r)\circ(u_rJ):Q_rF\to FP_r$ be the chosen-compactification exchange of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] (2), always using this same compactification. Then, naturally for $M\in D^b_c(X,A)$ and $m\geq1$,
$$v_{m+1,M}\circ d_{m,JM}=J(c_{m,M})\circ v_{1,P_mM}\circ B_1(v_{m,M}),$$
$$e_{m+1,M}\circ t_{m,FM}=F(c_{m,M})\circ e_{1,P_mM}\circ Q_1(e_{m,M}).$$
These are identities of the specified maps in the ambient pro-etale module derived categories, without any $k$-linearity assumption on the horizontal maps.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square] to $j_0$ and $r\geq1$: its Galois square is precisely the square with horizontal arrows $g^r,b^r$, so $jg^r=b^rj$ and it is Cartesian. The chosen lift is $(g^r,j)$: the two components are the horizontal and vertical arrows of that square. By [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian], $g$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^{-1})$. Its $r$-th power has inverse $(g^{-1})^r$. Thus all the horizontal maps used here are scheme maps; no assertion of $k$-linearity enters.

source.place: Galois-square paragraph; identification of the chosen lift from its two projections

proof.text: Because $\ell\ne p$, Bezout gives integers $u,v$ with $u\ell+vp=1$; in every local ring of the characteristic-$p$ scheme $X$, $u$ is an inverse of $\ell$. Apply the finite-coefficient case of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] to the isomorphism $g^r$ from Step 1, with coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and its constant-sheaf structure identification. Its conclusion puts $L(g^r)^*M$ in $D^b_c(X,A)$ whenever $M$ is in that category. In particular $P_mM$ is a permissible constructible input in the displayed equations.

source.place: Finite-coefficient isomorphism pullback, as made precise by lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback; agent specialization

proof.text:
Use the normalized canonical exchange of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] on the squares of Step 1. Paste first the square with arrows $g^m,b^m$ and then the square with arrows $g,b$ on its pullback side. The horizontal composites are $g^m\circ g=g^{m+1}$ and $b^m\circ b=b^{m+1}$. Contravariant pullback therefore gives $P_1P_m$ and $B_1B_m$. The pasting clause of that lemma, using the inverse composition comparisons $c_m,d_m$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], is exactly
$$v_{m+1,M}\circ d_{m,JM}=J(c_{m,M})\circ v_{1,P_mM}\circ B_1(v_{m,M}).$$
The lemma states both normalization on the open and pasting for these specified canonical maps on the pro-etale derived categories, so no replacement of $v_r$ by an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism occurs.

source.place: Final paragraph: pasting of Cartesian squares; specialize its canonical composition identifications

proof.text:
Expand the chosen-compactification recipe of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] (2), namely $e_{r,M}=R(v_{r,M})\circ u_{r,JM}$. Apply the proper-pasting equation assumed in the statement at $K=JM$, then Step 3 and functoriality of $R$:
$$\begin{aligned}
e_{m+1,M}\circ t_{m,FM}
&=R(v_{m+1,M}\circ d_{m,JM})\circ u_{1,B_mJM}\circ Q_1(u_{m,JM})\\
&=F(c_{m,M})\circ R(v_{1,P_mM})\circ R(B_1(v_{m,M}))\circ u_{1,B_mJM}\circ Q_1(u_{m,JM}).
\end{aligned}$$
Naturality of the specified transformation $u_1:Q_1R\to RB_1$, applied to the morphism $v_{m,M}:B_mJM\to JP_mM$ in the ambient category on $W$, says
$$R(B_1(v_{m,M}))\circ u_{1,B_mJM}=u_{1,JP_mM}\circ Q_1(R(v_{m,M})).$$
Substitute this equality, group the adjacent factors $R(v_{1,P_mM})\circ u_{1,JP_mM}=e_{1,P_mM}$, and use functoriality of $Q_1$ to group $Q_1(R(v_{m,M}))\circ Q_1(u_{m,JM})=Q_1(e_{m,M})$. This yields the claimed compact equation. These are the components of natural transformations throughout, hence the equality is natural in $M$. All intermediate objects are allowed in the ambient unbounded module derived categories; only the input $P_mM$ needs Step 2.
